P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but not read back: 'I know you spoke with Kim, he gave me like an overview, so I've got a little bit of a head start on you.' Same standing three-part frame, missing what's in the way and what you need. Agreement asked and given ('Alrighty?' / 'Alrighty. Cool.'). Open question delivered verbatim: 'What was it that you were hoping we could potentially help you out with, man?'

P2.evidence: Two of nine. Training status was asked properly — 'Are you kind of just on and off at the moment?' — producing 'I literally haven't worked out in probably about a year or two', and diet was asked directly. Everything else was skipped. No height, no weight, no age asked (27 was volunteered). Most seriously, not a single health or injury question was asked on a call that closed: no conditions, no hereditary history, no chronic pain, no movement limitations. The prospect volunteered shoulder and pec stiffness and loss of range, and it was met with agreement rather than a follow-up. No sleep, no energy, no results from prior training. A 27-year-old three weeks after a new baby, sedentary for two years, was sold six months of ballistic training without anyone establishing a single physical baseline.

P3.evidence: The best goals work in the batch. Surface goal asked ('If we were to fast forward six months, what is it you really want?'). The bridge was asked properly and produced the real trigger: 'you've had some sort of, I need to change moment, come to Jesus moment or something. I'm curious, what was that for you?' — answer, the three-week-old daughter and 'if I don't do it now, I'm never going to do it'. The deep question was reframed imaginatively and worked: 'the most perfect whole version of Andrew walks in that room... What would you say about the way that I've been approaching things?', which produced discipline, drained-ness, self-image and confidence. Legacy and identity were driven through to kids explicitly. And the reflect-back ran, cleanly: 'we'll use the goal as you showing up better rather than putting i want abs i want to lose this — put the goal as you showing up as the best version of you every day.' Missing only something-physical-you-cannot-do and a direct who-else-does-this-impact question.

P4.evidence: Past attempts and outcomes were largely volunteered rather than asked, which caps P4a and P4b at partial. But the root-cause work is the strongest in the corpus so far. The sabotage read was offered as an observation and landed: 'I've noticed something. This is gonna be a very deep question... It sounds like you sabotage a lot. Like, you get there and then you put yourself back down a little bit' / 'Yeah, that's true.' The blocker was named and owned by the prospect — information overwhelm and no accountability. And the information-is-not-the-problem move ran in substance throughout: 'you've just got some programs that just need to be rewired', against a prospect who holds a physical therapy assistant degree and already knows the anatomy.

P5.evidence: The fifth consecutive call in this batch with no consequence frame. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not'. The line in the sand ran — 'it all comes down to whether you feel like you're ready to jump into the discomfort' / 'here I am dude, here I am, I'm ready.' The emotional excavation in P3 partly substituted for it, but the specific move that makes inaction expensive was never made, and on this call it is what should have carried the household conversation: a prospect who could articulate the cost of two more years like this would have had something to take to his wife other than 'courage'.

P6.evidence: Belief question asked explicitly and before any number: 'I've got two questions for you, the first question is do you believe it's possible' / 'I do.' A clear readiness yes was obtained before the offer walkthrough — 'well if you feel like you're ready I can walk you through it' / 'yeah I'm ready'. The announced second question was never actually delivered; the conversation drifted into the religion exchange instead, so the all-in question — is there any reason you wouldn't go all in — was never asked. That omission matters here more than on any other call in the batch, because the answer was sitting in plain sight: he had no access to the money.

P11.evidence: Payment was collected on the call rather than deferred to a link, and the onboarding call with Trevor was genuinely booked live — Wednesday, afternoon, 3:15pm Pacific confirmed — which is the only completed P11b in the batch. The rep also offered that the wife could attend the onboarding call. No agreement email was mentioned and nothing was signed on the call; no welcome email, no Skool community link and no onboarding questionnaire. The Skool community omission is notable given the prospect asked for exactly that three separate times.

objection_plays.detail: This is the most important entry in the batch and it needs stating plainly: the play was run close to as written, and running it as written produced the outcome. Moves executed — the man-to-man permission frame; establishing she lacked the full picture ('does she know to the level of depth that you and I have been into about really what's going on?'); the she-would-not-want-you-worse-off move projected forward ('in five years time... she'll look back on this moment and go, I'm pretty glad that he went against me on that one'); and the permission-versus-ownership move, delivered as 'courage to put yourself first, and courage to commit'. The single move NOT run is the one the script provides as the safety valve — put down a deposit, go and talk to her, full refund if she says no. That fallback exists precisely for a refusal like this one, and skipping it was the difference between a deal that survives the week and a charge on an account the payer does not control. Two aggravating specifics the play has no answer for: the refusal here was not anticipatory, it had already happened, and the objection was quantified in household terms the rep never engaged with — more than their monthly house payment. Scored hit on adherence and flagged critical on conduct, deliberately. The lesson for the principal is not that this rep improvised; it is that OB has no stopping rule.

Money was on the table twice and the play never ran. First at 00:37:33: 'I have a 5,000 limit on my credit card, and that's sitting at zero. So I'll get my, I think she has better credit and she has a bigger credit card' — a stated ceiling below the price, met with 'We take care of it now if that's possible.' Second after the refusal, where the objection was explicitly financial. No isolation, no should-I-versus-how frame, no permission question, and none of the six financial-picture questions. The single probe attempted — 'will it put you in a really tough spot?' — got the equivocal 'Uh, not necessarily' and was not followed up. Most consequential of all: no payment plan was offered at any point, although this rep had structured 50/50 splits for two prospects two days earlier and the wife's objection was framed as a monthly-cost problem that a split would have directly addressed.

Fear and doubt were present throughout — 'I feel kind of stuck here', 'it's a frustrating spot I'm in right now', and the discomfort exchange before the pitch. The rep ran a good normalising frame ('it's going to be uncomfortable. There's not going to be any part of the journey that's going to be comfortable') and the not-your-fault-but-your-responsibility line, which landed well. None of the specific scripted images ran — no certainty question, no pleasure-versus-pain, no plane, no burned-before. 'Courage' was used as a general-purpose substitute for all of them.

notes: Two calls in one. Phases 3 and 4 are the best work by any rep in this batch — the sabotage observation, the perfect-version-of-Andrew question and the reflect-back are all textbook and all landed on a prospect who genuinely opened up. Then the same three structural weaknesses that run through every call in this folder converged at the worst possible moment: no baseline at all, so nobody knows anything about this man's body; no consequence frame, so there was no case to take to his wife except courage; and no financial-picture work, so a stated $5,000 ceiling and a joint account in someone else's name passed without comment. The coaching instruction is narrow and urgent: OB must terminate in the deposit-and-refund fallback when a spouse has already refused, and OC must run before a card is requested, not instead of it.
